With the OpenTelemetry Java agent attached through one environment variable and no code change, the lab joins each message's producer and consumer spans on its SQS message ID and counts how many share one trace ID, reads the AWSTraceHeader on a waiting message, and confirms a sample of traces in Splunk Observability Cloud.

files.content:
# Follow SQS messages through Splunk APM with the OTel Java agent and zero code

## What it shows

Two Spring Boot services run on EKS and exchange messages over a real Amazon SQS queue. `orders` sends each order with `SqsTemplate`, and `fulfilment` handles it with `@SqsListener`. Both use the same jar on the same image, and neither has any tracing code.

* `reproduce.sh` (BEFORE): installs the Splunk OTel Collector, builds the jar once in the cluster, and sends 400 orders with no agent. It also finds one waiting message on the queue by its ID, to show what a message carries by default.
* `fix.sh` (BUILD): sets one environment variable on each service and sends the same 400 orders. It joins each message's producer and consumer spans on the SQS message ID, reads the trace header from one message on the queue, and reads a sample of 10 traces back from Splunk Observability Cloud.

The headline number is how many messages have producer and consumer spans that share one trace ID, of those sent. The producer span is the publish span, and the consumer span is the process span: kind `CONSUMER`, named `<queue> process`. A message that doesn't join is reported as no process span, no producer span, or a different trace.

The run sets no SQS or messaging option. The agent writes the trace into the `AWSTraceHeader` message system attribute when it sends, and the lab shows that header on a waiting message next to the producer span's trace ID.

`fix.sh` then changes one setting on `fulfilment`, `otel.instrumentation.common.messaging.experimental.receive-telemetry.enabled=true`, and sends 100 more orders. It counts the process spans that stay in the producer's trace, and the ones with a span link to it. Default settings suit a reader who wants one trace per message, and receive telemetry suits one who wants each consumer in a trace of its own, linked to its producer.

Each run prints what decided its result: the jar and agent hashes, the agent version, and the receive telemetry and propagator settings on each pod. `console` and `logging-otlp` are on so the lab can count every message from the pod logs and read span links.

`@SqsListener` here takes one message at a time and polls up to 10 messages, set in `SPRING_CLOUD_AWS_SQS_LISTENER_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_POLL`. The results apply to this listener style. Spring Cloud AWS observation is left off.

## How the pods reach SQS

`main.tf` creates a role that may use this one queue, and EKS Pod Identity gives it to the `sqs-lab` service account. The pods hold no AWS keys, and the AWS SDK picks up the credentials through its default chain.

## Run it

Set `AWS_REGION`, `LAB_NAME`, `TF_VAR_lab_name` (the same value as `LAB_NAME`), `SPLUNK_REALM`, `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN` (ingest) and `SPLUNK_API_TOKEN` (read). Then run:

```bash
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
./reproduce.sh
./fix.sh
./cleanup.sh
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

The run uses two `t3.large` nodes, one SQS queue and an EKS control plane for about an hour.

`k8s/15-standin-sqs.yaml` and `check.sh` are for free checks only, where ElasticMQ stands in for SQS. A real run never applies that file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, run on a GitHub runner with Docker before AWS is paid for. It builds the lab's real source and runs it with the
# real agent against ElasticMQ, which stands in for SQS and keeps AWSTraceHeader. Kubernetes, Splunk and real SQS are not tested here.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
mkdir -p c/src c/out c/mq c/load

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
open("c/src/pom.xml", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "pom.xml"))
open("c/src/App.java", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "App.java"))
open("c/mq/elasticmq.conf", "w").write(block("k8s/15-standin-sqs.yaml", "elasticmq.conf"))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY

IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'maven:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
PY_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ ]+' k8s/20-load.yaml)
MQ_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'softwaremill/elasticmq-native:[^ ]+' k8s/15-standin-sqs.yaml)
AGENT_URL=$(grep -m1 -oE 'https://github.com/[^"]+\.jar' k8s/00-build.yaml)
QUEUE_URL=http://sqs:9324/000000000000/lab-orders
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== Fetching the agent and building the jar"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$PY_IMAGE" python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlretrieve('$AGENT_URL', '/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar')"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/src:/src:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  set -e; mkdir -p /w/src/main/java/lab; cp /src/pom.xml /w/; cp /src/App.java /w/src/main/java/lab/; cd /w
  mvn -q -B -DskipTests package; cp target/app.jar /lab/app.jar'
ls -l c/out

# grep reads the whole log here, because a grep that stops early breaks the pipe and pipefail would report that as no match.
logged() { docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep "$2" >/dev/null; }

docker run -d --name sqs --network lab -v "$PWD/c/mq/elasticmq.conf:/opt/elasticmq.conf:ro" "$MQ_IMAGE" >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 30); do logged sqs 'ElasticMQ server (.*started' && break; sleep 1; done
logged sqs 'ElasticMQ server (.*started' || { docker logs sqs 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: the stand-in didn't start"; exit 1; }

start() {   # service, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
  docker run -d --name "$1" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab:ro" --entrypoint java \
    -e "SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=$1" -e QUEUE_NAME=lab-orders -e AWS_REGION=eu-central-1 -e SPRING_CLOUD_AWS_SQS_LISTENER_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_POLL=10 \
    -e SPRING_CLOUD_AWS_SQS_ENDPOINT=http://sqs:9324 -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=standin -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=standin \
    -e "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=$2" "$IMAGE" -Xms256m -Xmx256m -jar /lab/app.jar >/dev/null
}
ready() {
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do logged "$1" 'process running for' && break; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'process running for [0-9.]+' | tail -1 | sed "s/^/$1 /"
  logged "$1" 'process running for' || { docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -40 | cut -c1-240; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1; }
}
load() { docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e "MESSAGES=$1" "$PY_IMAGE" python /load/load.py; }
drained() {   # how many orders fulfilment must report
  handled=0
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    handled=$(docker logs fulfilment 2>&1 | fulfilled_count)
    [ "$handled" -ge "$1" ] && break
    sleep 1
  done
  echo "fulfilled: $handled of $1"
  [ "$handled" -ge "$1" ] || { docker logs fulfilment 2>&1 | tail -30 | cut -c1-240; echo "CHECK FAILED: not every order was handled"; exit 1; }
}
collect() {
  docker logs orders > c/orders.log 2>&1
  docker logs fulfilment > c/fulfilment.log 2>&1
  count_shared c/orders.log c/fulfilment.log
  count_links c/fulfilment.log
  echo "$1: producer spans $produced, consumer spans $consumed, joined $joined, sharing one trace $shared, distinct traces $traces, linked to the producer $linked, most process spans for one message ${most:-0}"
}
probe() {   # sets header, with fulfilment paused so the message waits on the queue
  docker stop -t 20 fulfilment >/dev/null
  docker rm fulfilment >/dev/null
  docker exec orders curl -sS --max-time 20 -X POST "http://localhost:8080/orders/$PROBE_ORDER" | tee c/probe.json
  echo
  docker exec orders curl -sS --max-time 20 -H 'Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0' -H 'X-Amz-Target: AmazonSQS.ReceiveMessage' -d "$(peek_body)" http://sqs:9324/ > c/peek.json
  found=$(pick_message "$(jq -r '.messageId' c/probe.json)" < c/peek.json)
  [ -n "$found" ] || { cut -c1-300 c/peek.json; echo "CHECK FAILED: the probe message wasn't on the queue"; exit 1; }
  header=$(jq -r '.Attributes.AWSTraceHeader // empty' <<<"$found")
  echo "AWSTraceHeader on the message: ${header:-none}"
}

AGENT="-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.metrics.exporter=none -Dotel.logs.exporter=none"
ORDERS="$AGENT -Dotel.traces.exporter=console -Dotel.service.name=orders"
FULFILMENT="$AGENT -Dotel.traces.exporter=console,logging-otlp -Dotel.service.name=fulfilment"

echo "== No agent"
start fulfilment ""
start orders ""
ready fulfilment
ready orders
load 60 | tee c/before.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' c/before.txt || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30 | cut -c1-240; echo "CHECK FAILED: orders failed with no agent"; exit 1; }
drained 60
collect "no agent"
probe
[ -z "$header" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: a message carried a trace header with no agent"; exit 1; }
docker rm -f orders >/dev/null

echo "== With the agent on its defaults"
start fulfilment "$FULFILMENT"
start orders "$ORDERS"
ready fulfilment
ready orders
docker logs orders 2>&1 | grep 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' || true
load 100 | tee c/after.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' c/after.txt || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30 | cut -c1-240; echo "CHECK FAILED: orders failed with the agent"; exit 1; }
drained 100
sleep 7
collect "default run"
{ grep -m1 ' PRODUCER \[' c/orders.log || true; } | sed -E 's/^.*LoggingSpanExporter - //' | cut -c1-420
{ grep -m1 ' CONSUMER \[' c/fulfilment.log || true; } | sed -E 's/^.*LoggingSpanExporter - //' | cut -c1-420
[ "$shared" -eq 100 ] || { head -5 spans-joined.txt; echo "CHECK FAILED: $shared of 100 messages shared one trace"; exit 1; }
[ "$traces" -eq 100 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: expected one trace per order, got $traces"; exit 1; }
[ "$most" -eq 1 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: a message got $most process spans"; exit 1; }

probe
root=$(trace_root <<<"$header")
sleep 2
docker logs orders > c/orders-probe.log 2>&1
id=$(jq -r '.messageId' c/probe.json)
span_trace=$(span_rows PRODUCER c/orders-probe.log | awk -v m="$id" '$1 == m {print $2}')
echo "trace ID in the header: ${root:-none}, on the producer span: ${span_trace:-none}"
[ -n "$root" ] && [ "$root" = "$span_trace" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the header doesn't carry the producer's trace"; exit 1; }

echo "== One setting changed: receive telemetry on, on fulfilment only"
start fulfilment "$FULFILMENT -Dotel.instrumentation.common.messaging.experimental.receive-telemetry.enabled=true"
ready fulfilment
docker rm -f orders >/dev/null
start orders "$ORDERS"
ready orders
load 40 | tee c/receive.txt
drained 40
sleep 7
collect "receive telemetry run"
[ "$joined" -eq 40 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: joined $joined of 40"; exit 1; }
[ "$shared" -lt 40 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the setting changed nothing"; exit 1; }
[ "$most" -eq 1 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: a message got $most process spans"; exit 1; }
{ grep -m1 '"scopeSpans"' c/fulfilment.log || true; } | cut -c1-300
[ "$linked" -eq 40 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: $linked of 40 process spans link to the producer"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: one environment variable on each service. Same jar, same image, same Collector, same queue, no code change.
# Then join each message's producer and process spans on its SQS message ID, and read a sample of traces back from Splunk.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=830
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_fixed; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_fixed"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_API_TOKEN is not set"
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"
queue_settings

# The whole change. console and logging-otlp print spans to the pod log as well as sending them, so the lab can count every message and read links.
options() {   # service, exporters, then any extra setting
  echo "-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$1 -Dotel.exporter.otlp.endpoint=http://\$(HOST_IP):4318 -Dotel.resource.attributes=deployment.environment=$LAB_NAME,deployment.environment.name=$LAB_NAME -Dotel.logs.exporter=none -Dotel.traces.exporter=$2${3:+ $3}"
}

echo "== 2. The before-check: the cluster's own data reaches Splunk while the services send nothing"
cluster=0
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 150 500)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
  sleep 15
done
echo "cluster metric time series in Splunk: ${cluster:-0}"
[ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no cluster data reached Splunk, so a zero here would prove nothing"

echo "== 3. The whole change: one environment variable on each service, and no SQS setting among its values"
kubectl -n demo set env deployment/orders "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=$(options orders otlp,console)" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the variable on orders"
kubectl -n demo set env deployment/fulfilment "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=$(options fulfilment otlp,console,logging-otlp)" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the variable on fulfilment"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/fulfilment --timeout="$(cap 120 450)s" >/dev/null || { why fulfilment; fail "fulfilment did not roll out"; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 450)s" >/dev/null || { why orders; fail "orders did not roll out"; }
for s in orders fulfilment; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar)"
  echo "$s agent jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar)"
  kubectl -n demo logs "$p" -c app 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' | sed "s/^/$s /"
  effective "$s"
done
[ "$(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}')" = "$(cat jar-sha.txt)" ] && echo "jar unchanged from the before run" || fail "the jar changed, so the comparison would be unfair"

echo "== 4. The same 400 orders, with the agent on its defaults"
load_run 400 load-after.txt "$(cap 170 400)"
sleep 8
collect after
echo "default run: sent $sent, fulfilled $handled, producer spans $produced, consumer spans $consumed, joined on message ID $joined, sharing one trace $shared, distinct traces $traces"
echo "default run, misses: no process span $no_consumer, no producer span $no_producer, different trace $different. Most process spans for one message: ${most:-0}"
one_trace_pct=$(awk -v s="$shared" -v n="$sent" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", s * 100 / n}')
echo "one trace percent, default run: $one_trace_pct"
echo "default run, consumer spans linked to the producer: $linked"
echo "-- three of the joined rows: message ID, producer trace, consumer trace"
awk 'NR <= 3 {print "  " $0}' spans-joined.txt
echo "HERO_MEASURE: messages_sent[default]=$sent"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: one_trace_messages[default]=$shared"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: one_trace_percent=$one_trace_pct"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: consumer_spans_linked_to_producer[default]=$linked"
default_sent=$sent
default_shared=$shared
awk '$2 == $3 {print $2}' spans-joined.txt | sort -u | awk 'NR % 40 == 1' > sample-traces.txt

echo "== 5. How the trace crossed the queue: fulfilment pauses, one order goes in, and that message is read from the queue"
probe
with_header=$(grep -c . <<<"$header" || true)
echo "default run, messages carrying the header: $with_header"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: trace_header_on_message[default]=$with_header"
sleep 3
kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest orders)" -c app > orders-probe.log 2>/dev/null
span_trace=$(span_rows PRODUCER orders-probe.log | awk -v m="$probe_id" '$1 == m {print $2}')
root=$(trace_root <<<"$header")
echo "trace ID in the header: ${root:-none}, on the producer span: ${span_trace:-none}"
matches=$([ -n "$root" ] && [ "$root" = "$span_trace" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)
echo "trace header root matches the producer span: $matches"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: trace_header_root_matches=$matches"
resume "$(cap 90 300)"

echo "== 6. One setting changed: receive telemetry on, on fulfilment only, for 100 orders"
SETTING=-Dotel.instrumentation.common.messaging.experimental.receive-telemetry.enabled=true
kubectl -n demo set env deployment/fulfilment "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=$(options fulfilment otlp,console,logging-otlp "$SETTING")" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the option"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/fulfilment --timeout="$(cap 90 280)s" >/dev/null || { why fulfilment; fail "fulfilment did not roll out"; }
effective fulfilment
load_run 100 load-receive.txt "$(cap 60 240)"
sleep 8
collect receive
echo "receive_telemetry run: sent $sent, fulfilled $handled, joined on message ID $joined, sharing one trace $shared, in their own trace $different. Most process spans for one message: ${most:-0}"
echo "receive_telemetry run, consumer spans linked to the producer: $linked"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: messages_sent[receive_telemetry]=$sent"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: one_trace_messages[receive_telemetry]=$shared"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: consumer_spans_linked_to_producer[receive_telemetry]=$linked"

echo "== 7. What Splunk Observability Cloud shows for the default run"
map=""; services=0; both=0; checked=$(grep -c . sample-traces.txt || true); : > confirmed.txt
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 420 25)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  map=$(topology)
  services=$(jq -r '[.data.nodes[]?.serviceName // empty] | length' <<<"$map" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  for t in $(cat sample-traces.txt); do
    grep -q "^$t\$" confirmed.txt && continue
    items=$(trace_items "$t")
    [ "$(jq -r '[.[].serviceName] | index("orders") != null and index("fulfilment") != null' <<<"$items" 2>/dev/null)" = true ] && { echo "$t" >> confirmed.txt; last=$items; }
  done
  both=$(grep -c . confirmed.txt || true)
  echo "  t+$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s: services=${services:-0} sampled traces holding both services=$both of $checked"
  [ "${services:-0}" -ge 2 ] && [ "$both" -ge "$checked" ] && break
  sleep 20
done
jq -r '.data.nodes[]? | "  \(.serviceName) inferred=\(.inferred // false)"' <<<"$map" 2>/dev/null || true
jq -r '.data.edges[]? | "  \(.fromNode) -> \(.toNode)"' <<<"$map" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "services on the map from Splunk: ${services:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: services_on_map=${services:-null}"
if [ "$both" -ge 1 ]; then
  echo "-- trace $(awk 'NR == 1' confirmed.txt) from Splunk APM"
  jq -r '.[] | "  \(.serviceName) \(.operationName)"' <<<"${last:-[]}" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | awk 'NR <= 12'
fi
echo "sampled traces with both services in one trace in Splunk: $both of $checked"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_traces_both_services=$both"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_traces_checked=$checked"

if [ "$(( default_shared * 100 ))" -ge "$(( default_sent * 95 ))" ] && [ "$both" -ge 1 ] && [ "${services:-0}" -ge 2 ]; then
  emit fixed
else
  emit not_fixed
fi

# Shared by the lab's scripts. Sourced, never run on its own.
export LC_ALL=C
PROBE_ORDER=999999    # the one message read from the queue by hand, kept out of every count

standin() { [[ "${LAB_NAME:-}" == rehearsal-* ]]; }    # true only in the free rehearsal, where ElasticMQ plays SQS

queue_settings() {
  if standin; then
    QUEUE_NAME=lab-orders
    QUEUE_URL=http://sqs:9324/000000000000/lab-orders
  else
    QUEUE_NAME=$(terraform output -raw queue_name)
    QUEUE_URL=$(terraform output -raw queue_url)
  fi
}

# "<message ID> <trace ID>" for spans the agent printed. The producer span is the publish span of kind PRODUCER.
# The consumer span is the process span: kind CONSUMER, named '<queue> process'. A receive span is never counted.
span_rows() {   # kind, log files
  local kind=$1 name=""
  shift
  [ "$kind" = CONSUMER ] && name=" process"
  { grep -h LoggingSpanExporter "$@" || true; } |
    sed -nE "s/.*'[^']*$name' : ([0-9a-f]{32}) [0-9a-f]{16} $kind \[.*messaging\.message\.id=([0-9a-fA-F-]+).*/\2 \1/p" | sort -u
}

# Joins producer and consumer spans on the SQS message ID. Sets produced, consumed, joined, shared, traces and the three ways a message can miss.
count_shared() {   # log files
  span_rows PRODUCER "$@" > spans-producer.txt
  span_rows CONSUMER "$@" > spans-consumer.txt
  join spans-producer.txt spans-consumer.txt > spans-joined.txt
  produced=$(cut -d' ' -f1 spans-producer.txt | sort -u | wc -l)
  consumed=$(cut -d' ' -f1 spans-consumer.txt | sort -u | wc -l)
  joined=$(cut -d' ' -f1 spans-joined.txt | sort -u | wc -l)
  shared=$(awk '$2 == $3 {print $1}' spans-joined.txt | sort -u | wc -l)
  traces=$(awk '$2 == $3 {print $2}' spans-joined.txt | sort -u | wc -l)
  most=$(cut -d' ' -f1 spans-consumer.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | awk 'NR == 1 {print $1}')
  no_consumer=$(( produced - joined ))
  no_producer=$(( consumed - joined ))
  different=$(( joined - shared ))
}

# Consumer process spans with a link to the producer's trace, from the OTLP JSON the agent prints, because the console format leaves links out.
count_links() {   # log files. Needs spans-producer.txt, and sets linked.
  { grep -h '"scopeSpans"' "$@" || true; } | sed -E 's/^[^{]*//' |
    jq -Rr 'fromjson? | .scopeSpans[]?.spans[]? | select(.name | endswith(" process")) | ([.attributes[]? | select(.key == "messaging.message.id") | .value.stringValue][0]) as $m | .links[]? | "\($m) \(.traceId)"' |
    sort -u > spans-links.txt
  linked=$(join spans-links.txt spans-producer.txt | awk '$2 == $3 {print $1}' | sort -u | wc -l)
}

# Distinct orders a log says were handled. Reads stdin, and the probe message doesn't count.
fulfilled_count() {
  { grep -oE 'fulfilled "?order-[0-9]+' || true; } | { grep -v "order-$PROBE_ORDER\$" || true; } | sort -u | wc -l
}

# The request body that reads waiting messages and their system attribute. A visibility of 0 leaves them on the queue.
peek_body() {
  jq -cn --arg q "$QUEUE_URL" '{QueueUrl: $q, MessageSystemAttributeNames: ["AWSTraceHeader"], MaxNumberOfMessages: 10, VisibilityTimeout: 0, WaitTimeSeconds: 5}'
}

pick_message() { jq -c --arg id "$1" '[.Messages[]? | select(.MessageId == $id)] | first // empty' 2>/dev/null; }    # reads stdin

trace_root() {   # "Root=1-69fa1b2c-0123456789abcdef01234567;Parent=..." becomes the 32 hex digit OTel trace ID
  sed -nE 's/.*Root=1-([0-9a-f]{8})-([0-9a-f]{24}).*/\1\2/p'
}

# ---------- the rest is for reproduce.sh and fix.sh, on Kubernetes ----------
newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }
why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -8 | cut -c1-120; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -10 | cut -c1-180; kubectl -n demo logs deploy/"$1" -c app --tail=25 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-220; }

load_run() {   # message count, file for the output, seconds to wait. Sets sent and handled.
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e "s/value: \"400\"/value: \"$1\"/" k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$3s" || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; why orders; fail "the load did not finish"; }
  kubectl -n demo logs load | tee "$2"
  sent=$(grep -oE 'sent=[0-9]+' "$2" | cut -d= -f2)
  [ "${sent:-0}" -gt 0 ] || { why orders; fail "no order reached the queue"; }
  local i
  handled=0
  for i in $(seq 1 18); do
    handled=$(kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest fulfilment)" -c app 2>/dev/null | fulfilled_count)
    [ "$handled" -ge "$sent" ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
}

collect() {   # label. Saves both services' logs, then counts the join and the links.
  kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest orders)" -c app > "orders-$1.log" 2>/dev/null
  kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest fulfilment)" -c app > "fulfilment-$1.log" 2>/dev/null
  count_shared "orders-$1.log" "fulfilment-$1.log"
  count_links "fulfilment-$1.log"
}

queue_depth() {   # visible messages, printed for the record
  if standin; then
    kubectl -n demo exec deploy/orders -c app -- curl -sS --max-time 20 -H 'Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0' -H 'X-Amz-Target: AmazonSQS.GetQueueAttributes' \
      -d "$(jq -cn --arg q "$QUEUE_URL" '{QueueUrl: $q, AttributeNames: ["ApproximateNumberOfMessages"]}')" http://sqs:9324/ | jq -r '.Attributes.ApproximateNumberOfMessages // "unknown"'
  else
    aws sqs get-queue-attributes --queue-url "$QUEUE_URL" --attribute-names ApproximateNumberOfMessages --query Attributes.ApproximateNumberOfMessages --output text
  fi
}

# Pauses fulfilment, sends one order, and finds that exact message on the queue by its ID. Sets header and probe_id.
probe() {
  local i found=""
  kubectl -n demo scale deploy/fulfilment --replicas=0 >/dev/null || fail "could not pause fulfilment"
  kubectl -n demo wait --for=delete pod -l app=fulfilment --timeout=60s >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  echo "messages waiting before the probe: $(queue_depth)"
  kubectl -n demo exec deploy/orders -c app -- curl -sS --max-time 20 -X POST "http://localhost:8080/orders/$PROBE_ORDER" | tee probe.json
  echo
  probe_id=$(jq -r '.messageId // empty' probe.json 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$probe_id" ] || fail "the probe order was not sent"
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
    if standin; then
      kubectl -n demo exec deploy/orders -c app -- curl -sS --max-time 20 -H 'Content-Type: application/x-amz-json-1.0' -H 'X-Amz-Target: AmazonSQS.ReceiveMessage' -d "$(peek_body)" http://sqs:9324/ > peek.json
    else
      aws sqs receive-message --queue-url "$QUEUE_URL" --message-system-attribute-names AWSTraceHeader --max-number-of-messages 10 --visibility-timeout 0 --wait-time-seconds 5 --output json > peek.json
    fi
    found=$(pick_message "$probe_id" < peek.json)
    [ -n "$found" ] && break
  done
  [ -n "$found" ] || fail "the probe message $probe_id was not found on the queue"
  header=$(jq -r '.Attributes.AWSTraceHeader // empty' <<<"$found")
  echo "message $probe_id AWSTraceHeader: ${header:-none}"
}

resume() {   # seconds to wait
  kubectl -n demo scale deploy/fulfilment --replicas=1 >/dev/null || fail "could not resume fulfilment"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/fulfilment --timeout="$1s" >/dev/null || fail "fulfilment did not resume"
}

# What decided the result, read from each pod rather than assumed. A setting that isn't present is at the agent's default of false.
effective() {   # service
  local opts
  opts=$(kubectl -n demo get "$(newest "$1")" -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[0].env[]? | select(.name == "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS") | .value')
  echo "$1 receive telemetry: $(grep -oE 'receive-telemetry\.enabled=[a-z]+' <<<"$opts" || echo 'not set, default false')"
  echo "$1 propagator for messaging: $(grep -oE 'use-propagator-for-messaging=[a-z]+' <<<"$opts" || echo 'not set, default false')"
  echo "$1 OTEL_ environment variables: $(kubectl -n demo get "$(newest "$1")" -o json | jq '[.spec.containers[0].env[]?.name | select(startswith("OTEL_"))] | length')"
}

# Reads from the Splunk Observability Cloud API for fix.sh. Sourced, never run on its own. Needs API and SPLUNK_API_TOKEN.
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

topology() {   # Splunk's Go client sends start/end in epoch milliseconds. ISO times are tried second.
  local now range body out
  now=$(jq -rn 'now | floor')
  for range in "$(( (now - 1500) * 1000 ))/$(( now * 1000 ))" "$(jq -rn --argjson n "$now" '$n - 1500 | todate')/$(jq -rn --argjson n "$now" '$n | todate')"; do
    body=$(jq -cn --arg t "$range" --arg e "$LAB_NAME" '{timeRange: $t, tagFilters: [{name: "sf_environment", operator: "equals", scope: "GLOBAL", value: $e}]}')
    out=$(curl -sS --max-time 20 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$body" "$API/v2/apm/topology" 2>/dev/null)
    jq -e '.data' <<<"$out" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  done
  echo "$out"
}

trace_items() {   # every span Splunk holds for a trace: the newest segment, then each segment, because a queue can split a trace in time
  local seg
  {
    curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/latest" 2>/dev/null | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . else [] end' 2>/dev/null
    for seg in $(curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/segments" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if type == "array" then .[] else empty end' 2>/dev/null); do
      curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/$seg" 2>/dev/null | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . else [] end' 2>/dev/null
    done
  } | jq -cs 'add // []' 2>/dev/null
}

# Free checks only. ElasticMQ stands in for Amazon SQS during the rehearsal, and a real run never applies this file.
# It keeps the AWSTraceHeader system attribute, as SQS does, so the rehearsal takes the agent's default path.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: sqs-standin
  namespace: demo
data:
  elasticmq.conf: |
    include classpath("application.conf")
    node-address {
      protocol = http
      host = "*"
      port = 9324
      context-path = ""
    }
    rest-sqs {
      enabled = true
      bind-port = 9324
      bind-hostname = "0.0.0.0"
      sqs-limits = strict
    }
    queues {
      lab-orders {
        defaultVisibilityTimeout = 30 seconds
      }
    }
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sqs
  namespace: demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: sqs }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: sqs }
    spec:
      nodeName: LOAD_NODE
      volumes:
        - name: conf
          configMap:
            name: sqs-standin
      containers:
        - name: sqs
          image: softwaremill/elasticmq-native:1.7.1
          ports:
            - containerPort: 9324
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: conf, mountPath: /opt/elasticmq.conf, subPath: elasticmq.conf }
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: 9324 }
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 60
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: sqs
  namespace: demo
spec:
  selector: { app: sqs }
  ports:
    - port: 9324

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Places one order every 50 ms. Each order is one HTTP request, and orders turns it into one SQS message.
    import http.client, os, time
    count, gap = int(os.environ["MESSAGES"]), 0.05
    conn, sent, errors = http.client.HTTPConnection("orders", 8080, timeout=30), 0, 0
    for order in range(1, count + 1):
        began = time.time()
        try:
            conn.request("POST", "/orders/%d" % order)
            reply = conn.getresponse()
            reply.read()
            ok = reply.status == 200
        except Exception:
            ok = False
            conn.close()
        sent, errors = sent + ok, errors + (not ok)
        time.sleep(max(0, gap - (time.time() - began)))
    print("LOAD sent=%d errors=%d" % (sent, errors))
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: MESSAGES, value: "400" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: orders sends each order to an SQS queue and fulfilment handles it with @SqsListener. The Collector runs and no agent is attached.
# This fixes the baseline: every message arrives, and the message itself carries no trace header.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=810
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_reproduced; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_reproduced"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
queue_settings
[ -n "$QUEUE_URL" ] || fail "no queue URL"

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes -o wide || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" || true

# The services stay on one node and the load on the other, in every run.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE"
echo "load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1) first, so it is running in every run"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" || fail "collector agent not ready"

echo "== 3. Building the jar in the cluster, once, and fetching the agent, unused for now"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
state=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 430 300)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  state=$(kubectl -n demo get job build -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$state" in *Complete*|*Failed*) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build --all-containers --tail=20 2>/dev/null || true
case "$state" in *Complete*) ;; *) kubectl -n demo describe job build | tail -15; fail "the build did not finish: ${state:-still running}" ;; esac
echo "build took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying orders and fulfilment with no agent"
if standin; then
  echo "free rehearsal: ElasticMQ stands in for Amazon SQS"
  sed "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" k8s/15-standin-sqs.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the stand-in"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/sqs --timeout="$(cap 90 180)s" || fail "the stand-in did not start"
  extra=(--from-literal=SPRING_CLOUD_AWS_SQS_ENDPOINT=http://sqs:9324 --from-literal=AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=standin --from-literal=AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=standin)
else
  extra=()
  echo "queue: $QUEUE_NAME in $AWS_REGION"
fi
kubectl -n demo create configmap sqs-env --from-literal=QUEUE_NAME="$QUEUE_NAME" --from-literal=AWS_REGION="$AWS_REGION" --from-literal=SPRING_CLOUD_AWS_SQS_LISTENER_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_POLL=10 "${extra[@]}" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not save the queue settings"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the services"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/fulfilment --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" || { why fulfilment; fail "fulfilment did not start"; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 160)s" || { why orders; fail "orders did not start"; }

echo "== 5. No agent is attached, and the image and jar are recorded"
for s in orders fulfilment; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or OTEL settings: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq '[.spec.containers[0].env[].name | select(test("^(JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS|OTEL_)"))] | length')"
  echo "$s jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar)"
  standin || echo "$s Pod Identity credential settings on the pod: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq '[.spec.containers[0].env[].name | select(. == "AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI")] | length')"
done
kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}' > jar-sha.txt
echo "agent jar, unused for now: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar)"
echo "listener: @SqsListener takes one String, so single-message mode, polling up to 10 messages. Spring Cloud AWS observation is not enabled."

echo "== 6. 400 orders, one every 50 ms, each one message on the queue"
load_run 400 load-before.txt "$(cap 170 90)"
kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest orders)" -c app > orders-before.log 2>/dev/null
kubectl -n demo logs "$(newest fulfilment)" -c app > fulfilment-before.log 2>/dev/null
count_shared orders-before.log fulfilment-before.log
echo "no_agent run: sent $sent, fulfilled $handled, producer spans $produced, consumer spans $consumed"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: messages_sent[no_agent]=$sent"

echo "== 7. What one message carries with no agent: fulfilment pauses, one order goes in, and that message is read from the queue"
probe
with_header=$(grep -c . <<<"$header" || true)
echo "no_agent run, messages carrying the header: $with_header"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: trace_header_on_message[no_agent]=$with_header"
resume "$(cap 90 5)"

emit reproduced
